pairs.why: Both push the magenta much hotter than the softer real backdrop, but B's background has lighter, more varied pink rings and slightly less saturated greens, so it sits a little nearer the real card.

A has a saturated yellow backdrop, a neutral grey floor and an orange hero, which matches the real cards' clear hue separation and rest areas. B is orange barrel on orange floor on pale yellow, so the whole card is warm.

B's hero carries real-card-level chroma, with a vivid green dome, a purple underside and orange lights against yellow. A's silver body and dull grey rim leave the hero less colorful than the real heroes.
A has the real card's mid-chroma blue body with cyan-ish cap highlights and a yellow-center to orange ray background. B's blue is more saturated and its orange-red rays are heavier.
A's green stripes are a mid green nearer the real cooler green, and its orange ring has some depth. B's stripes lean yellow-lime and its orange is flatter.
The two palettes are essentially identical: green grass, lavender-grey stone, navy and cream board, and a sandy path.

Both swap the real teal-to-purple muted backdrop for a bright cyan-to-royal-blue one. A adds a loud orange band that the real card doesn't have, while B keeps the housing a little darker and more purple-navy, so B is only marginally closer.
B keeps the real hue roles of green slide and support pole, blue ladder, yellow deck, pinkish tile and pale pool water. A turns the support poles blue and uses a heavier saturated blue pool.
